# windows_domain_membership (Resource)

Joins a remote Windows host to an Active Directory domain (`Add-Computer`) over SSH and PowerShell, and optionally unjoins it on destroy (`Remove-Computer`).

The Terraform resource ID is the lower-cased domain DNS name. The join credential travels to the host on stdin and never appears in the script body or logs.

A domain join only takes full effect after a reboot: `Add-Computer` is invoked **without** `-Restart`, and when `restart = true` a detached host reboot is scheduled ~60s after the join (likewise for the unjoin), so the reboot lands after Terraform records state. With `restart = false` (default), `pending_reboot` records the requirement and the host must be rebooted out-of-band.

`ou_path` and `server` are **create-only**: they are used for the initial `Add-Computer` call and never read back. Changing either later forces replacement (a new join) — the computer account is never moved in place.

**Destroy semantics:** by default destroy is a no-op (the host stays domain-joined). With `unjoin_on_destroy = true` the host is unjoined into `unjoin_workgroup_name` on destroy. The unjoin credential must come from the state-persisted `join_credential.password`: `password_wo` is WriteOnly and unavailable at destroy time, so that combination is rejected at plan time.

`Update` re-reads the live host to refresh the Computed attributes (`computer_name`, `pending_reboot`, `secure_channel_ok`) and therefore requires the host to be reachable — an unreachable host fails the update instead of silently keeping prior values.

The join credential needs domain rights to create or move the computer account in the target OU; without them the join is refused by the domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

variable "windows_host" {
  type = string
}

variable "windows_username" {
  type = string
}

variable "windows_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "domain_join_password" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "Domain account password for the join. Kept in state (Sensitive); use password_wo instead when destroy must stay a no-op."
}

# Minimal example: join the target host to corp.example.com.
# Add-Computer only queues the join; it takes full effect on the next reboot.
# With restart = false (default) the host must be rebooted out-of-band —
# surface pending_reboot to a downstream null_resource / windows_reboot
# module to orchestrate the reboot.
resource "windows_domain_membership" "this" {
  domain = "corp.example.com"

  join_credential = {
    username = "joiner@corp.example.com"
    password = var.domain_join_password
  }

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block create and
  # delete default to 15 minutes (a stalled domain-controller call surfaces
  # a timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely).
  timeouts = {
    create = "15m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "5m"
    delete = "15m"
  }
}

# Advanced example: place the computer account in a dedicated OU and
# schedule a detached host reboot ~60s after the join when a reboot is
# required (restart = true only takes effect when a pending reboot is
# reported). The OU and server are create-only: changing ou_path or server
# later forces replacement (a new join), never an in-place move.
resource "windows_domain_membership" "ou" {
  domain  = "corp.example.com"
  ou_path = "OU=Servers,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com"

  join_credential = {
    username = "joiner@corp.example.com"
    password = var.domain_join_password
  }

  restart = true
}

# Unjoin-on-destroy example: leaving the domain on destroy requires the
# state-persisted password (password_wo is WriteOnly and unavailable at
# destroy time, so that combination is rejected at plan time).
resource "windows_domain_membership" "ephemeral" {
  domain = "corp.example.com"

  join_credential = {
    username = "joiner@corp.example.com"
    password = var.domain_join_password
  }

  unjoin_on_destroy     = true
  unjoin_workgroup_name = "WORKGROUP"
}

output "domain_computer_name" {
  value       = windows_domain_membership.this.computer_name
  description = "Active computer name of the domain-joined host."
}

output "domain_pending_reboot" {
  value       = windows_domain_membership.this.pending_reboot
  description = "True when the target host must reboot to complete the join."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) DNS name of the Active Directory domain to join (e.g. `corp.example.com`). **ForceNew.** The resource `id` is the lower-cased form.
- `join_credential` (Attributes) Domain credential used for the join (and for the unjoin when `unjoin_on_destroy` is `true`). Exactly one of `password` / `password_wo` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--join_credential))

### Optional

- `ou_path` (String) Distinguished name of the OU for the computer account (e.g. `"OU=Servers,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com"`). **Create-only:** used for the initial `Add-Computer` call and never read back. Changing it later forces replacement (the computer account is never moved in place).
- `restart` (Boolean) When `true` and the join/unjoin leaves a pending reboot, schedule a detached host reboot ~60s after the operation (`shutdown.exe /r /t 60`), so the reboot lands after Terraform records state. When `false` and a reboot is required, `pending_reboot` is set and the host must be rebooted out-of-band. Default `false`.
- `server` (String) Optional domain controller (or domain) name passed to `Add-Computer -Server`. **Create-only:** changing it later forces replacement.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `unjoin_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, `terraform destroy` unjoins the host into `unjoin_workgroup_name` (`Remove-Computer`). Requires `join_credential.password` (the state-persisted password — `password_wo` is unavailable at destroy time). Default `false`: destroy is a no-op and the host stays domain-joined.
- `unjoin_workgroup_name` (String) Workgroup the host joins when `unjoin_on_destroy` unjoins it. NetBIOS rule: 1..15 chars, alphanumeric + hyphen, cannot start/end with a hyphen, cannot be purely numeric. Default `WORKGROUP`.

### Read-Only

- `computer_name` (String) Active computer name (`Win32_ComputerSystem.Name`). Informational only — never drives a diff.
- `id` (String) Terraform resource ID. Equal to the lower-cased domain DNS name.
- `pending_reboot` (Boolean) True when the OS exposes a pending reboot flag. Informational only — never drives a diff.
- `secure_channel_ok` (Boolean) `Test-ComputerSecureChannel` result. Informational only — never drives a diff (may be `false` while a join reboot is pending).

<a id="nestedatt--join_credential"></a>
### Nested Schema for `join_credential`

Required:

- `username` (String) Domain account for the join (UPN or `DOMAIN\user`). **ForceNew.**

Optional:

- `password` (String, Sensitive) Domain password. Sensitive on the wire but persisted in `terraform.tfstate`. Required (instead of `password_wo`) when `unjoin_on_destroy` is `true`, because the WriteOnly value is unavailable at destroy time. **ForceNew.**

The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only domain password (TPF v1.14+ WriteOnly). The plaintext is never persisted in `terraform.tfstate` — the framework drops it from state automatically. Cannot be combined with `unjoin_on_destroy` (the WriteOnly value is unavailable at destroy time). **ForceNew.**

The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time against the configured value): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing domain membership by the domain DNS name (lower-case).
# The host is verified to actually be joined to that domain. The join
# credential is never in state for password_wo, so set join_credential in
# configuration (and apply) after importing.
terraform import windows_domain_membership.this corp.example.com
```
